jobs.description:
Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.

The CFO will serve as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic advisor to the CEO/President and Board, providing leadership across financial planning, insurance accounting, capital and solvency management, investment portfolio performance, asset-liability management, treasury, risk, regulatory reporting, and corporate development.

The successful candidate will combine deep financial expertise with strong commercial and investment acumen and will be capable of operating in a highly regulated financial-services environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy & Executive Leadership

Develop and execute the organization's overall financial strategy.

Advise the CEO, President, and Board on financial performance, capital allocation, investment strategy, and enterprise value creation.

Translate corporate strategy into financial plans, budgets, forecasts, and measurable objectives.

Lead financial decision-making across insurance, investment, and corporate operations.

Establish strong financial governance and accountability across the organization.

2. Financial Planning, Budgeting & Performance

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning.

Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support strategic decisions.

Monitor revenue, profitability, expenses, capital efficiency, and operating performance.

Establish financial KPIs and executive dashboards.

Identify opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and shareholder returns.

3. Insurance Finance & Performance

Oversee financial management of insurance operations, including premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, and underwriting performance.

Monitor key insurance financial metrics including loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting profitability.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk teams to assess financial performance and emerging exposures.

Ensure appropriate financial treatment and reporting of insurance liabilities and reserves.

Support pricing, product profitability, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions from a financial perspective.

4. Investment Finance & Portfolio Management

Provide financial oversight of the organization's investment portfolio and investment activities.

Partner with the CIO/Chief Investment Officer and Investment Committee on portfolio strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, realized/unrealized gains, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted returns.

Evaluate investment opportunities and strategic asset-allocation decisions.

Ensure investment activities are aligned with the organization's liabilities, liquidity requirements, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.

5. Capital, Solvency & Balance Sheet Management

Lead capital planning and balance-sheet optimization.

Monitor solvency, capital adequacy, liquidity, leverage, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize the organization's capital structure and return on capital.

Assess the financial impact of major business, investment, and insurance decisions on capital requirements.

Work closely with Risk and Actuarial functions on capital and solvency assessments.

6. Asset-Liability Management (ALM)

Provide executive financial oversight of asset-liability management.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support development of ALM strategies and balance-sheet optimization initiatives.

Ensure appropriate financial stress testing and scenario analysis.

7. Treasury & Liquidity

Oversee treasury, cash management, liquidity planning, and banking relationships.

Maintain adequate liquidity to meet claims, operating obligations, investment commitments, and strategic requirements.

Optimize cash deployment and short-term investment strategies.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

Establish robust treasury policies and controls.

8. Regulatory & Financial Reporting

Ensure accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting to the Board, shareholders, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and consolidated financial statements.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Lead relationships with external auditors, regulators, actuarial advisers, tax advisers, and other professional stakeholders.

Maintain strong financial controls and governance frameworks.

9. Risk Management & Financial Controls

Establish effective financial risk-management frameworks.

Monitor exposure to market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, operational, interest-rate, and foreign-exchange risks.

Strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and governance processes.

Work closely with the CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and other executives to manage enterprise-wide financial risks.

Ensure appropriate stress testing and contingency planning.

10. Reinsurance & Capital Optimization

Provide financial oversight of reinsurance strategy and economics.

Evaluate the financial and capital implications of reinsurance arrangements.

Monitor reinsurance recoverables, counterparty exposure, and profitability.

Support optimization of risk transfer, capital efficiency, and balance-sheet resilience.

11. Corporate Development & Strategic Investments

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, and business expansion opportunities.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and investment cases.

Assess potential M&A opportunities and their impact on capital, solvency, earnings, and shareholder value.

Support negotiations with investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners.

12. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, banks, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Communicate financial performance, capital strategy, investment results, and business outlook to key stakeholders.

Support investor presentations, Board materials, and strategic financial communications.

13. Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize finance systems, reporting infrastructure, ERP platforms, and financial analytics.

Improve automation, data quality, forecasting, and management reporting.

Establish real-time visibility into financial, insurance, investment, and risk performance.

Drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

14. Leadership & Talent Development

Lead Finance, FP&A, Treasury, Accounting, Financial Reporting, Tax, and related functions.

Build a high-performing and commercially focused finance organization.

Develop finance leadership talent and succession plans.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and business partnership.

Key Performance Indicators

The CFO will be accountable for:

Revenue and earnings growth

Operating and net profitability

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Combined ratio / underwriting profitability

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow management

Balance-sheet optimization

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and financial reporting quality

Cost of capital

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant executive leadership.

Previous experience as CFO, Group CFO, Finance Director, VP Finance, Deputy CFO, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, asset management, investment management, banking, pensions, financial services, or a related regulated financial institution.

Strong understanding of insurance financial statements, investment portfolios, capital management, and regulatory requirements.

Proven experience managing complex balance sheets, liquidity, capital, and financial performance.

Strong experience working with Boards, regulators, auditors, investors, rating agencies, and senior executives.

Demonstrated experience in financial strategy, investment analysis, and capital allocation.

Preferred Experience

Experience as Group CFO within a diversified insurance or financial-services group.

Experience across both insurance and investment/asset-management businesses.

Experience with life insurance, general insurance, health insurance, pensions, or reinsurance.

Exposure to institutional investment portfolios and alternative investments.

Experience with M&A, strategic investments, capital raising, restructuring, or corporate transformation.

Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions or regulated markets.

Experience interacting with insurance regulators and rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is an advantage.

Relevant insurance, actuarial, investment, or risk-management qualifications are advantageous.

Core Competencies

Insurance Finance

Corporate Finance

Investment Finance

Capital & Solvency Management

Asset-Liability Management

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Financial Modeling

Risk Management

Regulatory Reporting

Insurance Accounting

M&A & Corporate Development

Capital Allocation

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Financial Transformation

Leadership Characteristics

The successful CFO will be:

Strategic, commercially minded, and financially rigorous

Highly analytical and investment-oriented

Experienced in highly regulated environments

Strong in capital and balance-sheet management

Comfortable engaging with Boards, regulators, investors, and rating agencies

Able to balance growth, profitability, liquidity, capital, and risk

An effective strategic partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, and Chief Actuary

Strong in complex financial decision-making

A transformational finance leader capable of building high-performing teams

Compensation

A competitive executive compensation package comprising base salary, performance-based incentives, executive benefits, and other benefits commensurate with experience and market benchmarks.

jobs.description:
Facet was founded in 2016 on the belief that objective, personalized financial advice is essential to living well. Our mission is to empower people to live more enriched lives by delivering a new standard of advice. By removing asset minimums, we provide holistic planning that goes far beyond investments to address every way money impacts life. Our team of CFP® professionals are at the core of our service and are empowered by our best-in-class support teams and proprietary technology platform. This model allows Facet to integrate advice into our members’ entire financial picture—all for an affordable, flat membership fee.

Our commitment to innovation and member success has earned national recognition, including being ranked the #1 Best Financial Advisory Firm 2025 by USA TODAY and named to Newsweek’s list of America’s Top Financial Advisory Firms 2025. With an A+ BBB Rating and a Trustpilot “Excellent” score (as of Sept. 16, 2025)*, we are proud to be redefining the industry for our members and our team alike.

Why Facet? The Future of Financial Planning

The Associate Financial Planner role at Facet is unlike any other in the industry. We’ve stripped away the "old way" of doing business—no cold calling, no commission-chasing, and no mountains of paperwork. We’ve created a role focused entirely on why you became a planner in the first place: to hone your craft and change lives.

What Makes This Role Different?

  • The Elite "Training Camp": We invest heavily in your personal growth. You will be directly mentored by senior leaders to unlock your full potential, turning this entry-level role into career insurance for the modern workforce.
  • Real-World Muscle Memory: Under the direct wing of a Director, Planning Team Lead, you will clear away the "administrative noise" for members while building the skills needed to guide people from thinking to doing.
  • Focus on Behavior, Not Just Numbers: You will master the "art of the subtext," learning to read unspoken family dynamics and manage member emotional blocks that algorithms can never replicate.

Your Impact & Responsibilities

  • As an Associate Financial Planner, you will support approximately 2 senior lead planners. Your time is balanced across three high-impact buckets:

Direct Mentorship & Growth (~50% of Time)

  • Directly onboard 2 of your own personal members each week with "live classroom" guidance and real-time support from your Director.
  • Shadow active planning sessions to learn how to explain complex topics in a simple, jargon-free manner.
  • Participate in cross-functional rotations within Member Experience (MX) and Trading & Investment Ops (TIO) to learn the full scope of firm operations.

Roadmap Architecture & Strategic Co-Building (~45% of Time)

  • Analyze incoming financial inputs—including data, statements, and tax returns—to independently identify interlocking financial opportunities and tax efficiencies.
  • Own the core decision-making for underlying financial strategies and map structural paths directly into our system.
  • Translate big-picture goals into bite-sized, tactical action items and next steps for members.

Proactive Member Care & Continuity Coordination (~5% of Time)

  • Act as the primary point of contact for members when lead planners are out of office, ensuring a continuous, warm relationship.
  • Review inbound messages and utilize our human-at-heart framework to address urgent questions or calm financial anxieties.

Who You Are

  • An Evolving Guide: You have natural emotional intelligence and a foundational drive to help people stop over-thinking their money.
  • Someone with a Startup Mindset: You possess exceptional agility, comfort with evolving software tools, and a drive to build features that have never been done before.
  • A Growth Seeker: You are eager to transition from a plan builder to an authoritative, empathetic guide through rapid skill advancement.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in financial planning or a related field.
  • CFP® designation or successfully passed the CFP® exam and within 60 days of satisfying the experience requirement to use the CFP®.
  • 0-2 years of experience in the financial services industry, customer success, or a high-growth startup environment.
  • Exceptional communication skills and the ability to collaborate in a high-trust, tech-enabled environment.

Benefits

  • $80,000 - $95,000 base salary plus bonus
  • Equity (ISO): It is important to us that all employees are shareholders in our mission.

About Accumulus Technologies

Accumulus Technologies helps life sciences companies reduce regulatory friction, shorten timelines, and lower execution risk across product development and lifecycle management—delivering measurable and transformational ROI. We support the full spectrum of regulatory engagements—strategy, submissions, and lifecycle management—spanning CMC, clinical and nonclinical content, labeling, commitments, post-approval changes, and reliance/work-sharing models. Our focus is on commercial impact: faster approvals, smoother post-approval change execution, fewer surprises, and tighter alignment between commitments and what teams can deliver. Our clients measure the value we bring in the tens of millions.

Role Overview

The Senior Product Manager will independently own complex, ambiguous product areas end to end—from identifying and validating the right problems to setting product direction, guiding delivery, driving adoption, and iterating based on evidence.

You will work directly with global health authorities, life sciences sponsors, regulatory operations professionals, internal subject matter experts, and Technology teams to uncover meaningful problems and develop scalable solutions. You will be expected to exercise strong product judgment, make clear recommendations—including when not to build—and remain accountable for whether the product changes user behavior and creates business value.

This is a hands-on role for a product leader who can move fluidly between strategy, customer discovery, rapid prototyping, analytics, and execution in a complex, regulated enterprise environment.

Product Strategy and Ownership

  • Independently own one or more strategic product areas, translating broad company goals into a clear product direction, and execution plan.
  • Develop a deep understanding of regulatory engagements, user workflows, market dynamics, and the technical and compliance constraints that shape the Accumulus Platform.
  • Frame ambiguous opportunities, evaluate alternatives, make principled prioritization decisions, and provide clear recommendations about what to build, what not to build, and why.
  • Continuously assess product direction based on user evidence, business priorities, platform strategy, technical feasibility, risk, and market change.
  • Articulate the value and future direction of the platform to internal leaders, customers, partners, and other market-facing audiences.

Discovery and Validation

  • Lead discovery directly with regulator, and sponsor users to uncover underlying needs, behaviors, constraints, and opportunities rather than relying on stated requirements alone.
  • Design and execute research plans, interviews, workflow studies, experiments, and concept tests that reduce uncertainty and test the most important product hypotheses.
  • Rapidly prototype possible solutions, place them in front of users, synthesize what is learned, and recommend whether and how Accumulus should proceed.
  • Combine qualitative insight, product data, market evidence, and technical input to make well-reasoned product decisions before and after launch.
  • Build trusted relationships with users and stakeholders while maintaining independent product judgment.

AI Product Leadership and AI-Native Ways of Working

  • Identify where AI can create meaningful user and business value, and distinguish those opportunities from use cases where AI would add unnecessary complexity or risk.
  • Lead discovery and validation of AI-enabled workflows with regulators and customers, with explicit attention to accuracy, trust, transparency, explainability, human oversight, privacy, security, and quality.
  • Partner with Technology and other stakeholders on build, buy, or partner decisions; model and data considerations; evaluation approaches; and the path from prototype to production.
  • Use AI fluently and responsibly in day-to-day product work, including research synthesis, analysis, product requirements, rapid prototyping, product analytics, and communication.
  • Help establish product practices for evaluating, monitoring, and improving AI-enabled capabilities after launch.

User Experience and Product Quality

  • Own the clarity, usability, and coherence of the end-to-end product experience; do not treat UX quality as a separate team's responsibility.
  • Use modern prototyping tools, including Figma and AI-assisted tools, to explore workflows quickly, gather feedback, and iterate before committing to development.
  • Translate discovery findings into intuitive workflows, interaction requirements, and implementation-ready product artifacts.
  • Work closely with frontend engineers and other Technology partners throughout implementation to preserve product intent and ensure a high-quality user experience.
  • Apply strong product and UX judgment without needing to be a visual designer.

Product Outcomes and Analytics

  • Define clear success measures for product initiatives, including adoption, engagement, workflow, quality, and business outcomes.
  • Partner with Technology and analytics stakeholders to ensure the product is instrumented appropriately and that the team can understand how users behave.
  • Monitor adoption and usage, investigate where expected behavior change is or is not occurring, and combine quantitative and qualitative evidence to determine next steps.
  • Use post-launch learning to improve the product, inform investment decisions, and determine whether to iterate, scale, reposition, or stop an initiative.

Execution and Delivery

  • Translate validated product direction into clear epics, user stories, workflows, acceptance criteria, and supporting artifacts that enable effective engineering execution.
  • Partner closely with Engineering in an agile environment to prioritize and refine the backlog, clarify intent, make scope and sequencing tradeoffs, and unblock delivery.
  • Identify cross-team dependencies, technical and product risks, and decision points early; present practical mitigation options and make timely tradeoffs.
  • Work in partnership with program management and business operations to support predictable, high-quality delivery across teams.
  • Ensure product issues identified during development or after release are understood, prioritized, and resolved appropriately.

Market, Regulatory, and Adoption Leadership

  • Stay informed about relevant regulatory expectations, industry standards, and market developments, and work with regulatory, legal, security, privacy, and quality partners to shape compliant solutions.
  • Serve as a product subject matter expert for internal teams, customers, prospective customers, partners, and market-facing communications.
  • Collaborate with product marketing, customer success, commercial, and operations teams on positioning, launch planning, enablement, adoption, and scalable operating processes.
  • Identify future growth opportunities and differentiated value propositions that advance Accumulus' mission and platform strategy.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or commensurate experience.
  • Seven or more years of product management experience, including a proven record of independently leading complex enterprise software products or product areas from discovery through delivery and iteration.
  • Five or more years of experience with enterprise SaaS platforms or supporting software in complex organizational environments.
  • Demonstrated strength in customer discovery, problem framing, hypothesis development, rapid experimentation, prototyping, and evidence-based product decision-making.
  • Strong product and UX judgment, with the ability to define coherent workflows and create prototypes without relying on a dedicated Product Designer.
  • Experience defining product success measures, partnering on instrumentation, analyzing adoption and usage behavior, and using qualitative and quantitative evidence to guide decisions.
  • Demonstrated AI-native ways of working and a practical understanding of the opportunities, limitations, risks, and responsible design considerations associated with AI-enabled products.
  • Strong technical fluency and the ability to collaborate effectively with Engineering on architecture, integrations, data, security, scalability, and delivery tradeoffs.
  • Experience shipping complex software through agile development processes while balancing user value, business outcomes, technical feasibility, compliance, and delivery risk.
  • Excellent written, verbal, facilitation, and formal presentation skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, executives, customers, and regulators.
  • Willingness to travel up to four times a year.

Strongly Preferred

  • Experience taking enterprise AI/ML or large language model capabilities from discovery and validation into production, including defining evaluation, human oversight, trust, and quality approaches.
  • Experience in life sciences, regulatory technology, healthcare, or another highly regulated software environment.
  • Experience with secure collaboration, content management, data exchange, regulatory submissions, workflow, or project management platforms.
  • Experience delivering product analytics, reporting, or self-service analytics capabilities.
  • A technical degree or hands-on software development, data, or systems integration experience.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Discretionary bonus = 15%

Our clinicians have the unique ability to customize the care for each and every individual patient. You will have the autonomy to determine how often you see a patient as well as the appropriate length of time spent with each patient. Medication management and individual psychotherapy are the most common forms of clinical work performed at OMH, but our clinicians also perform family therapy, group therapy, and psychological testing as needed and/or appropriate to a wide range of presenting problems of our patients.

Pick your own schedule!

  • Enjoy the freedom to create your own custom schedules with the perfect work/life balance.
  • Typically, clinicians work between Mondays – Fridays somewhere between the hours of 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM.

Focus on the patient’s care without the hassle or any additional on-call responsibilities. Simply cover the care for you own patients! Our medical staff and clinical psychotherapists focus on the patient’s care and our back-office support team handles the rest. This allows our clinicians time to be spent where it should be; with the patients they serve. Each clinician is responsible for clinical care and documentation following treatment sessions. Once that’s complete, our support team will handle all billing, collections, credentialing, etc. Once you leave the office for the day, your time is yours. No additional on-call responsibilities and no time spent wasted dealing with insurance companies.

Interested in benefits?

Full-time clinicians are eligible for medical health benefits. Please speak with the recruitment team to obtain additional specifics on benefits.

OMH is a growing, clinician-led company. Our Site Supervisors are geographically dispersed throughout the areas we work in order to have staff leaders available to every clinician. Talk with our recruitment team today about the advancement opportunities to become senior psychotherapists and/or site supervisors.

Licensure in Colorado and/or Massachusetts as a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner with experience working with persons who have various behavioral health issues such as, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, personality disorders, substance misuse, and other psychiatric impairments under the supervision of a consulting psychiatrist(s).  We welcome new graduates!

We bring deep expertise and a consultative mindset to everything we do—asking the right questions, challenging assumptions when needed, and always centering around our clients’ goals. In this role, you’ll be the subject-matter expert who frames the solution as part of the win-strategy for higher-ed web solutions engagements, helping prospective clients understand where they’re stuck and advising them on the right path forward, not just pitching a product.

We’re building toward a future where OHO is higher education’s most trusted advisory and implementation partner, and this role sits on the front lines of that journey—translating institutional challenges into smart, actionable web strategies.

About the Position

At its core, this role exists to win business: owning win-strategy, shaping the story OHO tells, engaging directly with clients, and leading pitches and proposals for Web Solutions deals.

The Principal Web Solutions Strategist sits on OHO’s Web Solutions Strategy team and plays a critical role at the intersection of business development, strategy, and delivery, in close partnership with the Director of Strategy. This role leads the strategic definition of Web Solutions deals, from early conversations with prospective clients through high-level involvement during delivery—ensuring that what OHO sells is thoughtful, viable, and aligned with how we deliver value.

In the sales process, the Principal Web Solutions Strategist crafts and communicates the vision and then defines the solution. You will own the majority of strategic airtime in client conversations:

  • Properly diagnosing client pain points and goals
  • Leading pitches and proposal strategy
  • Creating proposals and pitch materials, bringing in subject-matter experts and delivery leads when specialized input is needed or the opportunity requires a custom deliverable
  • Presenting audits and strategic recommendations
  • Clearly explaining OHO’s approach and the “how” behind our work

Proposal and pitch work is core to this role. It’s strategic work, not just production work. You’ll set the direction and narrative, developing customized proposals and pitch materials that communicate a persuasive, tailored solution that meets the client’s needs while effectively communicating the value OHO would bring to the engagement.

You’ll work closely with OHO’s Sales and Web Solutions teams, collecting collaborative input and feedback as you build the final proposal or pitch for delivery.

Through deep expertise in higher education websites and digital ecosystems, you’ll build trust quickly and confidently answer complex technical and strategic questions, partnering with OHO subject matter experts as needed.

After a project is won, you’ll stay engaged at key moments to ensure the project direction stays aligned with the vision established during the sales process. You’ll support a strong transition into delivery, participate in select milestones where your context is most valuable, and be available to help flag major strategic misalignments or risks so the team can address them early. This role provides continuity and confidence for the client at pivotal points while empowering the delivery team to lead day-to-day strategy and execution.

Beyond individual projects, you’ll help shape the evolution of OHO’s Web Solutions practice. You’ll gather market insights, identify buyer patterns, and partner with our Web Solutions leadership team to shape, inform and refine our offerings and how we talk about the value we bring to potential partners. i You’ll also contribute to OHO’s thought leadership so that OHO continues to be seen as a trusted strategic partner for higher education institutions.

Requirements

  • 7-10+ years of experience in digital strategy, web strategy, consulting, or agency environments.
  • Experience leading or owning delivery of digital projects in an agency and/or higher-education environment, with a solid understanding of how digital disciplines—UX, content strategy, design, and development—fit together and depend on one another. Higher-education experience is strongly preferred; candidates from other complex, highly regulated industries (e.g., healthcare, government, financial services) with comparable client and compliance dynamics are also encouraged to apply.
  • Deep expertise in content-intensive website strategy, including UX, content strategy, CMS platforms, accessibility, governance, SEO, and project delivery approaches.
  • Executive-level presence and strategic storytelling ability, with demonstrated comfort leading high-stakes pitches, setting vision, building trust with senior stakeholders, confidently owning the room, and influencing business development outcomes. This does not require a formal sales title or a traditional sales background.
  • Experience shaping, evolving, or stewarding service offerings or productized solutions.
  • Ability to balance pre-sale strategy leadership with high-level delivery involvement without becoming execution-focused.
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity and collaborating across sales, strategy, and delivery teams.
  • Strong judgment and decision-making skills, particularly around scope, approach, and strategic tradeoffs.
  • An intuitive problem-solver who can rapidly synthesize complex information, identify core problems, and pivot to strategic solutions with speed and precision.
  • Natural ability to rally teams, build momentum around a vision, and push deals or initiatives across the finish line.
  • Depth of technological understanding across diverse digital ecosystems, ensuring the ability to confidently advise on complex technical solutions and integrations.
  • Established or emerging thought leadership and external credibility—for example, conference speaking, published articles or perspective pieces, or a strong professional presence (e.g., LinkedIn) within the higher-ed or digital strategy community.

What Success Looks Like in 6–12 Months

Within 6–12 months, a successful Principal Web Solutions Strategist will:

  • Shape web opportunities so that by the time they’re late-stage, everyone is clear on the problem we’re solving, how success will be measured, and the recommended approach.
  • Develop and lead proposals and pitches that win, with measurable improvement in OHO's win rate on Web Solutions opportunities and wins increasingly driven by the strength of the strategy and story—not just price or scope.
  • Sell work that delivery teams describe as “right-sized and well framed,” with minimal need for major re-scoping once projects kick off.
  • Lead sales conversations that prospective clients and senior stakeholders regularly describe as advisory, clarifying, and confidence-building (for example, through direct feedback, NPS, or post-pitch debriefs).
  • Help evolve our Web Solutions offering by spotting patterns across deals and delivery and turning them into sharper packages, positioning, and case studies.
  • Become the person BDRs, BDMs, and Web Solutions Directors naturally pull into complex or ambiguous opportunities when they need help framing the problem and path forward.
  • Contribute to visible thought leadership in higher-ed web strategy (talks, webinars, articles, etc.) that we can point to as influencing new or stronger client relationships.

OHO Benefits

OHO offers a comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance package, along with company-paid life insurance as well as short/long-term disability coverage. Benefits also include a 401(k) match up to 4% of pay, paid vacation and sick time, ten holidays including a Flex Day, Summer Fridays, and more!

Each year, the team aims to come together in person for our Annual Summit at a beautiful destination, and throughout the year, leadership shares regular company updates and fosters an open-door culture. We also sprinkle in a healthy dose of fun with team events, friendly competitions, and other surprises that keep things fresh and connected.

Additional Information

Candidates should be comfortable traveling nationally 2-4 times a year for company and/or client meetings.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States in order to be considered. OHO is an e-Verify employer, ensuring compliance with federal employment eligibility requirements.

Today, we empower organizations to embrace transformation and leverage advanced technologies, including AI, to stay competitive. Pythian sits at the intersection of data engineering, AI production, and managed services — helping enterprises turn data complexity into competitive advantage. This means you’re never selling a point solution; you’re building long-term, high-value partnerships with clients who want a trusted advisor to help them scale intelligently.

If you’re energized by the AI transformation happening across enterprise technology right now, know how to sell complex managed services, and want to represent a company with deep technical credibility and a growing AI practice — this role is built for you.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.excerpt: ROLE PURPOSE As Senior Data Analyst, you turn iiDENTIFii’s data into decisions the business can act on with confidence.
jobs.description:
ROLE PURPOSE

As Senior Data Analyst, you turn iiDENTIFii’s data into decisions the business can act on with confidence. Business questions rarely arrive fully formed, so your craft is to shape a broadly worded question into something that can genuinely be answered, answer it well, and land that answer with the people who need to act on it.

This is a senior, hands-on analysis role that sits close to both the business and the data platform. You are comfortable interrogating a messy dataset in the morning and presenting a customer engagement analysis to leadership in the afternoon. You bring analytical depth, sound judgement on data quality and governance, and the communication skill to translate complex findings into decisions non-technical stakeholders can act on.

You work the lifecycle end to end: framing the question, modelling and interrogating the data, drawing out the insight, and seeing the recommendation through to a decision and its adoption. We care more about how well you think, how clearly you communicate and how curious you are about how data is built than about the particular tools you have used before. Strong analysts come from many backgrounds and industries, and we would like to hear from all of them.

What Good Looks Like in the First Six Months

  • You own the core business and client reporting, and the definitions behind those numbers are documented, consistent and trusted across teams
  • Recurring reporting that is rebuilt by hand today runs to a schedule, with quality checks attached
  • At least one piece of analysis you initiated, rather than were asked for, has changed a product, operational or commercial decision
  • Product, engineering and commercial treat you as the person to ask about what the data actually says

ROLE TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Reporting, Dashboards & Self-Service

  • Own end-to-end reporting for the key business metrics, keeping definitions consistent and trusted across teams
  • Build and maintain dashboards and self-service tools that let teams find and act on insight without going through you
  • Own recurring client reporting end to end: definition, automation, quality assurance, delivery and the follow-up conversation — credible explaining a number, or a discrepancy, directly to a client’s team
  • Handle ad-hoc requests with good judgement: establish the real question, deliver a clear and actionable answer, and prioritise sensibly when several arrive at once
  • Choose the tool that fits the purpose across our broad set of reporting and visualisation technologies, matching the right one to the audience, the question and the shelf life of the answer

Product & User Behaviour Analysis

  • Analyse user behaviour across our products to identify trends, friction points and opportunities, and turn findings into concrete recommendations
  • Track and report on engagement, retention and customer journey metrics, flagging risks and opportunities proactively rather than on request
  • Apply appropriate statistical rigour, including cohort analysis, significance testing, forecasting and seasonality, so that recommendations hold up when they are challenged
  • Design and evaluate experiments with product, and be clear about what a result does and does not prove
  • Investigate anomalies and unexpected patterns, and work out whether what you are seeing is genuine signal, a data quality issue, or noise

Automation & Data Foundations

  • Automate recurring analysis and reporting so that regular outputs run reliably to a schedule with quality checks, rather than being rebuilt by hand each cycle
  • Build and maintain your own analytical models and reusable assets on top of the curated data, so knowledge compounds instead of living in one-off queries
  • Specify what the analytics layer needs from upstream data (the sources, structures, definitions and refresh frequencies) and work with the engineering team to get there
  • Understand the data platform well enough to be a genuine partner to engineering: where data comes from, how it flows, and what an upstream change will mean downstream

Data Governance, Quality & Privacy

  • Work responsibly with personal and sensitive data under POPIA, with client obligations that can extend further — least-privilege access, aggregation and de-identification as a matter of course
  • Proactively identify and resolve data quality issues at the source, rather than patching around them downstream
  • Apply sound data security, governance and metadata management practices across pipelines, dashboards and datasets
  • Contribute to lean, practical data governance standards that balance rigour against the team’s pace of delivery

Stakeholder Engagement, Mentorship & Documentation

  • Partner with product, marketing, engineering and operations to ensure data is accessible, accurate and used effectively
  • Communicate technical and analytical concepts clearly and confidently to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Represent the analytics perspective alongside engineers, architects and leaders on the broader data platform roadmap
  • Mentor junior and intermediate analysts as the team grows, and contribute to internal training and knowledge sharing
  • Maintain clear documentation of data models, dashboards and workflows, so the team is never dependent on one person’s memory

AI-Augmented Ways of Working

  • Use AI as a standard part of your workflow: exploring data, drafting and optimising SQL, building and iterating on reports, writing documentation, and pressure-testing your own analysis
  • Build reusable AI workflows for your own work and share them with the team, so a repeatable analysis becomes a dependable automation rather than tribal knowledge
  • Keep a critical eye: verify AI output, know where it goes wrong, and never present a number you could not derive and defend yourself
  • Stay current with a fast-moving tooling landscape and bring what you find back to the team

Living the iiDENTIFii Culture

  • Champion iiDENTIFii’s culture and values in every interaction, and foster a team environment defined by intellectual rigour, psychological safety, collaborative excellence and a bias for action
  • Actively contribute to iiDENTIFii’s mission: powering innovators in remote biometric digital authentication, globally

QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS NEEDED

Experience

  • 5+ years as a Data Analyst or in a similar analytical role, with the depth and reliability that come with it
  • 5+ years of BI and data visualisation experience — we are deliberately tool-agnostic (Power BI, Looker, Tableau, Qlik or similar); what matters is that you have built things people actually use
  • A track record of delivering analytical work independently in an agile, fast-paced environment: scoping, estimating, delivering, and seeing it through to stakeholder sign-off while managing competing priorities
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics or a related field, or equivalent demonstrable experience
  • Exposure to a regulated or high-integrity environment (banking, insurance, telco, fintech, identity, risk or similar) is strongly advantageous — you will already understand why the numbers have to be right

Technical & Analytical Skills

  • Advanced SQL, and Python for analysis and automation
  • Strong applied statistics for analytical work: cohort analysis, significance testing, forecasting and seasonality
  • Experience with the Azure data stack (Data Factory, Synapse, Databricks) or an equivalent cloud data platform is valuable but not required
  • Familiarity with CI/CD, version control and modern development practices applied to analytics is advantageous
  • Experience with monitoring and observability tooling such as Application Insights, Azure Monitor or Grafana is a plus

Governance & Domain Knowledge

  • A working understanding of data security, governance and metadata management principles
  • Comfort working responsibly with personal and sensitive data in a compliance-conscious environment

Communication & Stakeholder Skills

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate insight into business impact for both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Experience presenting your own analysis to senior stakeholders
  • Experience presenting analysis directly to external clients is advantageous

Ways of Working

  • Comfortable owning work end to end, from framing a question through to seeing a recommendation adopted
  • Experience supporting or mentoring less experienced analysts is a plus

CULTURE AND BENEFITS

Why Join Us

iiDENTIFii is solving one of the most consequential technical problems in Africa’s digital economy: how do you verify that someone is who they say they are, remotely, at scale, across infrastructure that is inconsistent and high stakes? Our biometric identity platform is trusted by some of the continent’s most demanding institutions precisely because we have built something that works.

The analytics function here is small and growing. The foundations are in place — an expanding warehouse, established governance and data quality practices, reporting the business relies on. The gap now is capacity, not groundwork. There is more high-value analysis waiting than we have people to do it, and this role exists to change that.

Benefits

  • Your money works harder here. As an iiDENTIFii employee, you gain exclusive access to preferential banking benefits, including competitive rates on home loans, vehicle finance, and personal loans—delivering real financial value from day one.
  • Performance pays. Our competitive compensation package is designed to reward people who make an impact, because we believe exceptional work deserves exceptional recognition
  • Family comes first. We offer enhanced family responsibility leave, giving you the time and space that matters most when life calls
  • Your annual leave entitlement grows with your tenure
  • Cape Town-based preferred, with a remote-first culture
  • A technically excellent, mission-driven team at the frontier of biometric identity technology

jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY - RENEWABLE ENERGY SENIOR CORPORATE ATTORNEY

Clean Energy Counsel, a mission-driven law firm dedicated to accelerating the world’s transition away from fossil fuels, seeks to hire a highly qualified junior corporate associate with approximately 3 years of law firm experience and strong academic credentials to join our growing corporate practice. This attorney will work alongside experienced attorneys to advise clean energy companies, project developers, investors, private equity funds, and other clients on a broad range of sophisticated corporate and transactional matters.

The ideal candidate will have a strong foundation in corporate law and meaningful experience supporting complex business transactions, including mergers and acquisitions, equity financings, joint ventures, and other strategic transactions. Candidates should have excellent drafting, analytical, and organizational skills, with the ability to take ownership of discrete transaction workstreams and contribute effectively to deal teams.

This is an opportunity to join a collaborative, mission-driven law firm and work directly with sophisticated clients on transactions that support the continued growth of the clean energy economy.

This position is fully remote – as a distributed law firm, we offer the opportunity to work remotely from wherever you are licensed to practice law.

EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Approximately 3 years of corporate or transactional experience at a law firm, preferably with a strong corporate, M&A, private equity, or finance practice.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting complex corporate transactions, including mergers and acquisitions, equity financings, joint ventures, private equity investments, or other strategic transactions.
  • Experience drafting and reviewing transaction documents, conducting due diligence, preparing closing deliverables, and supporting transaction execution.
  • Strong foundational knowledge of corporate law, corporate governance, entity formation, and transactional structures.
  • Ability to independently manage assigned transaction workstreams, identify potential legal and business issues, and escalate complex matters appropriately.
  • Strong drafting, analytical, research, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, with excellent attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, organizational abilities, and the capacity to manage multiple assignments and competing deadlines.
  • A collaborative, team-focused approach and a willingness to learn from and work closely with senior attorneys.
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively in a fully remote work environment.
  • Admission to and in good standing with the Bar of the applicant’s state of residence.
  • Dedication to the Firm’s mission and an interest in developing expertise in renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure transactions.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support senior attorneys in advising clients on corporate and transactional matters throughout the business lifecycle.
  • Assist with mergers and acquisitions, reorganizations, restructurings, and other corporate strategic transactions.
  • Draft, review, and revise transaction documents related to equity financings, private equity investments, and other capital-raising transactions.
  • Assist with the structuring, documentation, and execution of joint ventures, strategic partnerships, and other commercial arrangements.
  • Support corporate governance matters, entity formations, capitalization structures, shareholder and partnership arrangements, and related corporate issues.
  • Conduct and coordinate legal due diligence, including reviewing organizational documents, material contracts, and other transaction-related materials.
  • Prepare and maintain transaction checklists, closing documents, ancillary agreements, and other materials necessary to facilitate successful transaction execution.
  • Coordinate with clients, opposing counsel, and other transaction participants on assigned matters, under the guidance of senior attorneys.
  • Identify legal and business risks, conduct research, and assist in developing practical solutions that advance clients’ objectives.
  • Manage assigned responsibilities and transaction workstreams efficiently while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.
  • Collaborate with attorneys across the Firm’s practice groups on multidisciplinary transactions.
  • Stay current on legal, regulatory, and market developments affecting corporate transactions and the clean energy industry.
  • Adhere to Firm policies, practices, and priorities.
  • Perform other duties as requested by Firm management.

BENEFITS

  • 1,200 annual billable-hour requirement, with bonuses for exceeding that requirement and for originating new clients and matters, based on a percentage of total revenue received.
  • Base salary of $190,000+. The base salary for this position will be determined during the interview process and will vary based on multiple factors, including but not limited to prior experience, relevant expertise, current business needs, and market factors.
  • Annual merit bonuses
  • Fully remote work environment with annual in-person retreat
  • 401(k), including firm profit-sharing matching
  • Dental/Health/Vision/Rx insurance
  • Paid time off and paid holidays

WHO WE ARE

At Clean Energy Counsel, we provide the legal power to get sustainable projects developed, financed, and built – because speeding our transition away from fossil fuels is how we change the world’s trajectory for the better. Our team of attorneys gets deals closed and projects built because we care. Advancing clean energy isn’t just our job—it’s our hope for the future. Clean Energy Counsel gives attorneys the opportunity to do sophisticated, meaningful, industry-advancing work, all while leading a more balanced life in a work culture that values collaboration and respect. For clients, this translates to an extraordinary level of care, brought to bear for a common cause. As the only mission-driven law firm solely focused on renewable energy, Clean Energy Counsel carries forward its unique model of advancing a sustainable future with sustainable law.

Our singular focus attracts the best talent in the industry, and we’ve built a deep and diverse bench of industry veterans who are passionate about their work and value our culture of respect and support.

We represent a diverse range of renewable energy project developers, investors, suppliers, and service providers across a full spectrum of technologies, including solar, energy storage, wind, energy efficiency, electric vehicles and charging infrastructure, waste-to-value, and sustainable infrastructure and materials - from Fortune 50 companies to start-ups.

COME AS YOU ARE!

Our deep-rooted commitment to diversity and inclusion drives our ability to attract high-performing attorneys with diverse experience and perspectives who value a supportive work culture based on care and respect. That includes providing equal employment opportunities without consideration of race, color, religion, ethnicity, citizenship, political activity or affiliation, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, sex or gender, or any other basis protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

Salary: 190,000+

jobs.description:
Η Würth Hellas, μέλος του διεθνούς Ομίλου Würth και μία από τις κορυφαίες εταιρείες στον χώρο των επαγγελματικών εργαλείων και λύσεων, αναζητά Remote Telesales Representative για την ενίσχυση της ομάδας πωλήσεων. Η θέση είναι 100% εξ αποστάσεως και απευθύνεται σε υποψηφίους από όλη την Ελλάδα. Μετά από πλήρως αμειβόμενη εκπαίδευση ενός μήνα στα κεντρικά γραφεία της εταιρείας, θα εργάζεσαι από τον χώρο σου, έχοντας στη διάθεσή σου όλα τα απαραίτητα εργαλεία και τη συνεχή υποστήριξη της ομάδας μας.

Αν αναζητάς μια σταθερή επαγγελματική ευκαιρία σε μια εταιρεία με ισχυρή παρουσία στην ελληνική και διεθνή αγορά, θα χαρούμε να σε γνωρίσουμε.

  • Διαχείριση και ανάπτυξη υφιστάμενου πελατολογίου επαγγελματιών.
  • Τηλεφωνική επικοινωνία με πελάτες για την παρουσίαση προϊόντων, νέων λύσεων και εμπορικών προτάσεων.
  • Διερεύνηση των αναγκών των πελατών και παροχή ολοκληρωμένων λύσεων.

  • Επίτευξη ποιοτικών και ποσοτικών στόχων.

Απαιτούμενα Προσόντα

  • Πολύ καλές επικοινωνιακές δεξιότητες.
  • Ευχέρεια στη διαχείριση πελατών και διαπραγμάτευση.
  • Εμπορική αντίληψη και πελατοκεντρική προσέγγιση.
  • Άνεση στη χρήση ηλεκτρονικού υπολογιστή και εφαρμογών Microsoft Office.
  • Οργανωτικότητα, συνέπεια και υπευθυνότητα.

  • Ομαδικό πνεύμα και διάθεση για συνεχή μάθηση.
  • Προϋπηρεσία σε πωλήσεις ή εξυπηρέτηση πελατών θα θεωρηθεί επιπλέον προσόν.

Benefits

jobs.excerpt: Design ManagerSupervisor: Director of EngineeringClassification: Full-time, exemptLocation: Full RemoteBenefits:· Competitive salaries· Health, vision and dental insurance· 401(k) program with 6% matching· Paid holidays· Flexible PTOPosition OverviewCalSolar is seeking a Design Manager to join our Engineering Team and serve as a client-facing technical leader for assigned commercial solar PV and battery energy storage projects throughout California.
jobs.description:
Design Manager

Supervisor: Director of Engineering

Classification: Full-time, exempt

Location: Full Remote

Benefits:

· Competitive salaries

· Health, vision and dental insurance

· 401(k) program with 6% matching

· Paid holidays

· Flexible PTO

Position Overview

CalSolar is seeking a Design Manager to join our Engineering Team and serve as a client-facing technical leader for assigned commercial solar PV and battery energy storage projects throughout California.

Reporting to the Director of Engineering, the Design Manager is responsible for managing the design and engineering execution of a portfolio of projects while leading a team of Designers and Drafters. This role serves as the primary coordination point between CalSolar and external project stakeholders, including developers, architects, engineers of record, general contractors, utilities, and building owners.

The Design Manager is accountable for ensuring project designs are technically sound, code-compliant, constructable, and delivered on schedule while maintaining strong client relationships throughout the project lifecycle.

Success in this role requires a unique combination of technical expertise, leadership ability, project management skills, and exceptional client-facing communication. The ideal candidate can confidently lead technical discussions, coordinate multidisciplinary teams, mentor junior staff, and build trust with clients and project partners.

Key Responsibilities

Client-Facing Technical Leadership

  • Serve as the primary technical point of contact for assigned clients and projects.
  • Lead design coordination meetings with developers, architects, engineers of record, general contractors, utilities, and project owners.
  • Manage technical communications throughout project development, permitting, and construction.
  • Develop trusted relationships with clients and project stakeholders.
  • Facilitate resolution of design challenges, scope changes, and technical conflicts.
  • Translate client objectives into actionable engineering and design deliverables.
  • Represent CalSolar professionally in stakeholder meetings, project reviews, and technical presentations.

Project Design Management

  • Manage the engineering and design execution of multiple commercial solar PV and BESS projects simultaneously.
  • Direct the preparation of permit plans, construction documents, utility interconnection packages, and engineering deliverables.
  • Coordinate internal design activities with project management, estimating, procurement, and construction teams.
  • Ensure projects maintain compliance with applicable codes, utility requirements, and client standards.
  • Perform quality reviews of engineering and drafting deliverables.
  • Support utility interconnection and AHJ permitting efforts.

Team Leadership

  • Lead and mentor a team of Designers and Drafters.
  • Assign workloads and manage project priorities within the team.
  • Provide technical guidance, coaching, and performance feedback.
  • Review design work for accuracy, quality, and consistency.
  • Support onboarding and professional development of engineering staff.
  • Promote engineering best practices and continuous improvement initiatives.

Technical Expertise

  • Review and coordinate:
  • Solar PV system layouts
  • Electrical single-line diagrams
  • Energy storage system designs
  • Equipment selections
  • Structural coordination requirements
  • Utility interconnection documentation
  • Identify and resolve constructability concerns early in the design process.
  • Support field teams with technical issue resolution during construction.
  • Contribute to the development of engineering standards, templates, and design procedures.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of commercial solar PV engineering, design, or project delivery experience.
  • Experience managing project stakeholders including developers, architects, engineers of record, contractors, and utilities.
  • Prior experience leading or mentoring Designers, Drafters, or engineering personnel.
  • Strong client-facing communication and relationship management skills.
  • Experience with commercial and multifamily solar projects, including both new construction and retrofit applications.
  • Experience coordinating permitting and utility interconnection processes within California.
  • Working knowledge of battery energy storage systems (BESS).
  • Strong understanding of NEC, California Building Code, California Fire Code, and commercial construction practices.
  • Excellent organizational, leadership, and project management capabilities.
Salary: $100,000 to $140,000

jobs.title: Distinguished Engineer, AI Security Systems
jobs.excerpt: As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations.
jobs.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.


About the Lab:

AI is changing cyber offense and defense simultaneously. Adversaries use models to inspect code, hunt vulnerabilities, adapt tooling, and conduct longer operations. CrowdStrike built the Cybersecurity Superintelligence Lab to ensure defenders stay ahead.


The Lab is CrowdStrike’s frontier AI research organization for cyber defense. Its work spans frontier and open-weight models, CrowdStrike-trained models, specialized agents, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and secure deployment.


The Lab combines trillions of Falcon events each day, more than a decade of adversary intelligence, expert-validated outcomes, and high-fidelity environments where offensive and defensive AI can attack, defend, learn, and prove what works in real enterprise environments.


About the Role:

We are seeking a Distinguished Engineer who has built AI and security systems that operate in the real world and stop real adversaries.


You may have worked on the endpoint, where every millisecond, megabyte, and CPU cycle matters, or at cloud scale, where systems reason over trillions of events and design decisions affect cost, latency, and efficacy across millions of protected assets. Ideally, you understand both.


As one of the Lab’s most senior technical leaders, you will architect systems that turn frontier AI into autonomous, trustworthy cyber defense—from the sensor to the cloud. You will write code, design experiments, set technical direction across research and engineering teams, and carry breakthroughs into the Falcon platform.


If you have shipped AI that stops adversaries in production and want to build what comes next, we want to talk.


What You’ll Do:

  • Architect the Lab’s AI security systems end to end, including models, agents, security telemetry, tools, execution environments, on-sensor inference, and cloud-scale reasoning.
  • Bring frontier AI to the endpoint using distillation, quantization, compact and specialized models, and integration with kernel- and user-mode telemetry.
  • Build cloud-scale streaming detection and inference systems across trillions of events per day, with GPU-efficient serving, intelligent model routing, and disciplined control of cost, latency, and reliability.
  • Build autonomous defenders that investigate, hunt, write and validate detections, and drive response and remediation.
  • Create systems that learn from investigations, adversary emulation, simulations, expert feedback, reinforcement learning, post-training, reward modeling, and synthetic data.
  • Engineer for adversarial conditions, including evasion, poisoning, prompt injection, tool abuse, sandboxed execution, and autonomous action in customer environments.
  • Establish benchmarks, cyber ranges, and evaluation harnesses measuring efficacy, false-positive cost, reliability, latency, and spend.
  • Lead through technical depth by working on the hardest problems, mentoring principal-level engineers and research scientists, and aligning cross-functional teams.
  • Carry research into production in the Falcon platform, solving the scale, safety, and operability challenges required for customer-grade capabilities.
  • Represent CrowdStrike through publications, open-source work, standards, and collaboration with frontier AI labs, universities, and the security research community.


What You’ll Need:

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field; PhD preferred.
  • 15+ years of industry experience in software engineering, machine learning, or security engineering; 12+ years with a PhD.
  • 8+ years at a senior technical leadership level, such as Principal, Distinguished, or equivalent.
  • A track record of architecting, building, and shipping production AI or ML systems for security, on the endpoint or at cloud scale.
  • Hands-on expertise with large language models and agentic architectures, including planning, tool use, memory, context management, post-training, reward modeling, and inference optimization.
  • Deep security expertise in areas such as detection and response, threat hunting, malware analysis, vulnerability research, adversary tradecraft, or security automation.
  • Expert-level proficiency in one or more of C, C++, Rust, Go, or Python.
  • Deep experience with distributed systems, high-throughput data infrastructure, and GPU inference stacks such as vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, or SGLang.
  • Scientific rigor and the ability to form hypotheses, establish credible baselines, design meaningful experiments, and follow the evidence.
  • A record of setting technical vision, raising the bar for senior engineers and researchers, and communicating complex tradeoffs clearly.
  • Proven experience using AI technologies to improve decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, increase efficiency, and drive business outcomes.


Bonus Points:

  • Cybersecurity industry experience across endpoint, cloud, identity, SIEM, or threat intelligence.
  • Experience at a frontier AI lab in pre-training, post-training, reinforcement learning, inference, evaluation, or safety.
  • Experience with adversarial machine learning, AI red teaming, autonomous cyber reasoning systems, or AI-driven offensive security.
  • Experience building extensible AI or agentic platforms that enable teams to safely develop, evaluate, optimize, and deploy AI applications at scale.
  • Recognized technical contributions, including publications, patents, influential open-source projects, or conference talks spanning AI and security.


Why Join the Lab:

  • Work on frontier technology with real-world consequences, protecting organizations that keep economies, hospitals, and critical infrastructure running.
  • Access trillions of daily Falcon events, deep adversary intelligence, and high-fidelity cyber environments.
  • Help define the technical culture, architecture, and standards of a new frontier lab.
  • Collaborate with AI researchers, offensive operators, threat hunters, and incident responders who understand how real attacks happen and how they are stopped.

Benefits of Working at CrowdStrike:

  • Market leader in compensation and equity awards

  • Comprehensive physical and mental wellness programs

  • Competitive vacation and holidays for recharge

  • Paid parental and adoption leaves

  • Professional development opportunities for all employees regardless of level or role

  • Employee Networks, geographic neighborhood groups, and volunteer opportunities to build connections

  • Great Place to Work Certified™ across the globe

jobs.description:
Title: Director, Advancement

Department: Advancement

Status: Exempt

Reports To: Vice President of Advancement

Remote position, Preference given to New York City and/or Metro

Summary

The Director, Advancement is a key member of the National Psoriasis Foundation’s Advancement team, responsible for building and growing relationships with individual donors and prospects to expand philanthropic support for NPF’s mission. This position manages a portfolio across annual, major, and planned giving, with a strong emphasis on developing meaningful donor relationships, securing significant philanthropic commitments, and building a robust pipeline for future growth.

The Director combines frontline fundraising with strategic planning and collaboration, working closely with Advancement leadership, executive leadership, board members, health care professionals, volunteers, and colleagues across NPF to connect donors with the programs, research, and priorities that are most meaningful to them.

As NPF prepares for a future capital campaign and seeks to significantly expand philanthropic investment in its mission, the Director will play an important role in strengthening donor relationships, developing the philanthropic pipeline, and advancing the fundraising practices and infrastructure needed to achieve ambitious organizational goals.

Portfolio Management & Relationship Building

  • Manage and grow a portfolio of individual donors and prospects across annual, major, and planned giving.
  • Identify and qualify prospective donors with the capacity, inclination, and connection to make meaningful philanthropic investments in NPF.
  • Build strong, personalized relationships by understanding each donor’s connection to NPF, philanthropic interests, and motivations for giving.
  • Conduct meaningful donor visits, virtual meetings, and personalized outreach to deepen engagement and advance relationships.
  • Develop and execute strategic moves management plans that guide donors and prospects through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Build and maintain a robust pipeline of qualified prospects to achieve current revenue goals and support long-term individual giving growth.

Major & Planned Giving

  • Cultivate, solicit, and secure significant philanthropic commitments from individuals and families, including five-, six-, and seven-figure gifts, as appropriate.
  • Partner with the Vice President of Advancement, Chief Development Officer, CEO, board members, health care professionals, and volunteers to develop and execute strategies for key donors and prospects.
  • Identify and promote planned and legacy giving opportunities, including bequests, beneficiary designations, charitable gift annuities, and other appropriate giving vehicles.
  • Leverage NPF events, programs, and mission experiences as strategic opportunities to cultivate relationships, advance solicitations, and deepen donor engagement.
  • Develop compelling giving opportunities that connect donor interests with NPF’s mission, programs, research, and strategic priorities.
  • Support NPF special events through strategic donor and honoree engagement, particularly when honorees, event leaders, or key participants are part of the Director’s portfolio or donor relationships.

Donor Engagement & Stewardship

  • Develop personalized stewardship strategies that demonstrate impact, strengthen donor relationships, and inspire continued and increased philanthropic support.
  • Collaborate with Research, Advocacy, Patient Support, Marketing, and other teams to create meaningful opportunities for donors to experience and understand the impact of NPF’s work.
  • Connect donors with NPF leadership, researchers, health care professionals, programs, and volunteer leaders based on their interests and engagement goals.
  • Ensure timely and appropriate donor recognition, impact reporting, and stewardship for portfolio donors and prospects.
  • Serve as a collaborative partner across the Advancement team, sharing donor insights and identifying opportunities to strengthen relationships and maximize philanthropic engagement across NPF.

Strategic Planning & Administration

  • Partner with the Vice President of Advancement on individual giving strategy, prospect development, portfolio management, and campaign readiness.
  • Contribute to Advancement planning, budget development, revenue forecasting, and the establishment of annual fundraising goals.
  • Monitor portfolio performance, pipeline activity, donor engagement, and fundraising outcomes to identify opportunities, assess progress, and inform strategy.
  • Maintain accurate and timely donor records, engagement plans, moves management activity, and opportunities within NPF’s CRM.
  • Use donor and fundraising data to strengthen portfolio strategy, inform decision-making, and support a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure fundraising activities reflect industry best practices and NPF policies, procedures, and standards.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Five to seven years of successful nonprofit fundraising experience in major gifts, planned giving, or individual giving.
  • Demonstrated success securing and closing five- and six-figure gifts
  • Experience managing a donor portfolio and moving prospects through the cultivation and solicitation cycle.
  • Knowledge of planned giving principles and legacy fundraising strategies.
  • Strong relationship-building, interpersonal, and networking skills.
  • Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation communication abilities.
  • Experience working with volunteers, board members, and senior leaders.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills with attention to detail.
  • Experience with Raiser's Edge, Salesforce, or comparable donor management systems preferred.
  • Experience with health-related nonprofit organization(s) preferred.
  • Ability to travel locally in New York and surrounding areas as needed.

Key Performance Indicators

  • Assigned portfolio revenue achieved/goal met.
  • Advancement department revenue achieved.
  • Planned gift commitments secured.
  • Portfolio activity metrics (visits, calls, proposals, and solicitations).
  • Proactive prospecting activity to identify, research, and qualify new individual giving prospects.
  • Number of qualified prospects added to portfolio.
  • Donor retention and upgrade rates.
  • Event-related and non-event fundraising and donor engagement outcomes.
  • Pipeline growth and movement through cultivation stages.
